Name: 0_young maiden_maiden_hay_bride

['I sing a song about a horse

Tail like linen fibers

To look at the Sõrve maiden

If only she were the honey to me  
What is riding past on the road  
Riding along the path  
The horse is like an oven  
The rider is like the day itself  
Her belt is like a rainbow  
Hat like a king’s crown  
My dear little brother  
If you go to take a wife  
Go catch a little sail  
Go court a little sparrow  
Take me under your belt  
Turn me into a six-sleeved coat  
I know a gloomy maiden  
I guess a bad maiden  
Gloomy maiden, long hair  
Lazy maiden, long braid  
A slender belt dripping  
Angry black eyebrows  
My dear little brother  
Don’t take a tall wife  
Tall ones go to sleep on a bench  
Don’t take a big wife  
Big ones tend to sulk  
Take a very small one  
A tiny little steel one  
A little diligent crazy one.', 'Virgin young maiden  
Slender at her writing desk  
Why do you hesitate when coming to me  
Coming to me; coming to me  
To me, a young man  
To me, proud of my good genes  
To the copper belt, white dawn  
Because you hesitate when coming to me  
Coming to me; being with us  
To me, a young man  
To me, proud of my good genes  
To the copper belt, white dawn  
That our yard is muddy  
The cowsheds full of holes  
Oxen treading in our yard  
The cows have slept heavily  
Foals playfully running around  
The maiden walks with the ox  
The maiden walks on the dry heath  
Walk along the edge of the garden  
Until you come to our yard  
Because you hesitate when coming to me  
Coming to me; being with us  
To me, a young man  
To me, proud of my good genes  
To the copper belt, white dawn  
That our wells are far away  
Water five versts (3.3 km each) away  
Do not complain, maiden  
The oxen will bring the water  
The reins will pull the cart  
Servants will bring the tub  
Will put the kettle on the fire  
Because you hesitate when coming to me  
Coming to me; being with us  
To me, a young man  
To me, proud of my good genes  
To the copper belt, white dawn  
That you have many debts  
More than pearl beads  
You think to pawn them  
To borrow bread  
To waste money  
To take grains  
To send salt  
You will not pawn those  
No bread will be borrowed  
No salt will be sent  
We will be thirsty at the foot  
When the harvest is poor  
The man’s gun will bring catch  
Do not hesitate when coming to me  
Coming to me; being with us  
We have large fields in the fields  
And wide strips in the forest  
Edges run down to the brook  
Sides reach the sea  
Corners to the gray meadow  
If you are, if you are a maiden  
If you are quick to pick  
Swift to take by hands  
Then your crown will carry gold  
Your head will carry a lace cap  
Your neck will carry a golden necklace  
Crown with golden ribbons  
Shoulders with pearl beads  
Hips with a half skirt  
Shins with silk stockings  
Feet with new shoes  
If you are, if you are a maiden  
If you are quick to pick  
Swift to take by hands  
Then you will feel the thimbleberries  
Your side will feel the rowans  
Shoulder blades the apple trees  
Forearms the maples  
Thighs like rowan bushes.', 'For I thank my aunt  
She gave soap to make clearer.  
To make foam whiter  
The day gave time to wash the head  
The moon to dry the hair  
I put the spruce to dry  
To sway in the apple tree  
To shine in the pines  
The spruce dried with golden hair  
The apple tree with silver hair  
The pine with gray hair  
The boys of Albu barked  
The boys of Sõidla rode around  
They thought the moon would shine  
The day gently shine  
The stars sparkle in the sky  
Those were my white hairs  
They wanted to crop my head  
To shorten the flaxen hair  
I gave to crop the head  
To shorten the flaxen hair  
Now Hans comes from Harju too  
Now Jaak from Järva too  
Peeter from long Piibe too  
They have scissors in hand  
Shears in the pocket too  
But they crop my head  
Shorten the flaxen hair  
Hans brings shoes with hooks  
Jaan brings shoes with leather straps  
Siim brings shoes with spikes  
I throw Hans’s shoes into the oven  
I throw Siim’s shoes in the shit  
I put Jaan’s shoes on my feet  
Then westward with shoes to the church  
Shoes click underfoot  
Laces snap behind  
Hair stands on the head  
Goes up to the armpits  
Sways over the shoulders  
I pass through the men’s men  
I slip also through the boys  
Albu boys are kind brothers  
Don’t think  
That I will become a bad woman  
Become one bad, stay one bad  
Become a kind one or maybe old  
Not even a whole parish  
I will become a woman on the Narva road  
A slippery woman on the city road  
A suitable woman in Paide  
My husband over the seas  
Drinks there at river’s edge  
Under the bluish-gray bridge  
Under the watery-gray mill  
Under the church of lavender  
I cannot ride to say  
To make a place for him  
To turn at the pillowcase  
The wind takes him entirely away  
The cloud pulls him  
What a life I have  
The life of a mistress I have  
The daughter of a lady’s lap  
She comes with a carriage after me  
Rides a sledge at seven  
Drives the horse at nine  
Already from that we get by three  
That we started well  
Let us finish comfortably']

Name: 2_cranes_lords_pasture_oxen
Representative_Docs:
['If it were up to me  
Secondly, my doing  
I would know what I would do  
I would make the gentlemen oxen  
Kilts cranes  
Maidens as necklaces  
I would go behind to call  
Plow the field, pour the grain  
Do not furrow the old red  
Turn the head of the brindle  
I went on Tuesday to the fair  
I had a piece of hay against the grain  
A patch of bog at the edge  
A patch of wet at the hill’s edge  
I would plow against the grain  
I would not ruin the ridges of the rye  
I would not spoil the shoots of the grass horns', 'If I were to be myself,  
If I were to become myself,  
Oh, I would know what I would do.  
I would make the gentlemen oxen,  
The ladies would wear bonnets,  
German girls would be servant maids,  
The rowdy ones would be stumblers,  
The proud ones behind cranes,  
I myself would be the caller behind:  
Plow the furrow, pour the story,  
Go straight, old red one!  
My plowman plows, the bend bends,  
My slope plows, the foot slips,  
My bridle plows, the head trembles,  
The dark one did lift the land indeed.', 'If it were my being,  
And secondly my doing,  
I would surely know what I would know:  
I would make the oxen into oxen,  
The horses into horses,  
The helpers into fathers,  
The boys into proud cranes,  
The girls into blossoms...  
I myself would be in the field,  
Plowing the furrow in the meadow,  
Letting the songs ring out,  
And the words be lovely to hear.  
Then the village would listen,  
The parish would watch closely,  
The forest would roar back,  
The grove would respond,  
Young women would smile,  
Men would ponder their thoughts,  
Children would quietly spy,  
Squatting by the village gate,  
Near the backyard of the household.  
Oh! If only it were my being,  
And secondly my doing;  
Surely I would know what I would know.']

Name: 3_sea_beneath_cuckoo_shore
Representative_Docs:
["What is here beneath our yard  
The sea beneath our yard  
What is in the middle of the sea  
A well in the middle of the sea  
What is on the edge of the well  
A post on the edge of the well  
What is at the very end of the post  
A sieve at the very end of the post  
What is on the edge of the sieve  
A cuckoo on the edge of the sieve  
What is on the cuckoo's hands  
A child was on the cuckoo's hands  
What is on the child's chest  
A brooch on the child's chest  
What is on the edge of the brooch  
A ring on the edge of the brooch  
Even this is a soldier's ring  
How did it come to this land  
From the knees of a chimney sweep boy  
From the shin bones of a German soldier", 'Rowing boat and reaching boat  
Reach beneath our yard:  
What is there beneath our yard?  
The sea is there beneath our yard.  
What is there in the middle of the sea?  
A post is there in the middle of the sea.  
What is on top of the post?  
A ring is on top of the post.  
What is inside the ring?  
Cuckoo’s feet are inside the ring.  
What messages does the cuckoo bring?  
The cuckoo brings war messages.  
Who among the three of us goes to war?  
Does the father go, or does the mother go,  
Or does the eldest son go?  
Neither the father goes, nor the mother,  
Nor does the eldest son go.  
The youngest brother goes to war.  
The sister went to teach the brother:  
“Don’t always ride ahead of the war  
Nor ride behind the war.  
Ride into the middle of the war!  
The first are thrown away,  
The last are killed,  
The middle ones return.”  
---------------  
I row beneath father’s door.  
“Hello, father, know your son,  
Know your son’s gray horse!”  
“Oh my God, I cannot know  
The son nor the gray horse.”  
I row beneath mother’s door.  
“Hello, mother, know your son,  
Know your son’s gray horse!”  
“Oh my God, I cannot know  
The son nor the gray horse!”  
I row beneath brother’s door.  
“Hello, brother, know me,  
Know my gray horse.”  
“Oh my God, I cannot know  
The brother nor the gray horse!”  
I row beneath sister’s door.  
“Hello, sister, know your brother,  
Know your brother’s gray horse.”  
“Oh my God, yes I can know!  
Come inside, sit down,  
Tell me stories about the war!”', 'What is there beneath our yard  
The sea beneath our yard  
What is in the middle of the sea  
A pillar in the middle of the sea  
What is at the end of the pillar  
A sieve at the end of the pillar  
What is inside the sieve  
A ring inside the sieve  
What is inside the ring  
A cuckoo inside the ring  
What does the cuckoo bring us  
It brings news of war  
Whose turn is it to go to war  
Will father go, or will mother go  
Or will the one who is swinging hidden go  
Sister went to teach brother  
Ride to the middle of the war  
The first are thrown out  
The last are killed  
The middle ones come home']

Name: 4_evening_night_moon_morning
Representative_Docs:
['Evening comes, arrives late  
The day rolls down low,  
Evening comes unexpectedly  
Twilight comes uninvited,  
Evening comes accompanied by the outdoors  
Twilight comes with the grain,  
Evening brings straw to the barn  
Twilight puts to sleep,  
The spirit awakens,  
Turns up the dawn  
And spreads the white wide.  
When this sieve stands on its edges,  
The poles against the white side,  
When dawn breaks on the Koigi side  
And whitens from the Varangu side,  
Then we are sent to work:  
One there, another here,  
Some to the manor fields.  
Slave labor is sought  
Wage workers are thrown in.  
If nothing else, to carry mud,  
To clear stones in the field,  
To roll stones together,  
To place stones in position.  
Shoes break the stone quarry,  
The stones place the stones in rows,  
Charcoal remains in the skirt.', "Sisters, dear ones  
Where are we going toward the night  
Toward the night, toward the day  
Let’s go listen to the moon  
Let’s play all day  
Let’s touch the gentle evening  
Does the moon serve without oil,  
The day contemplates pleasure  
The evening recites a hymn.  
No, the moon does not serve without oil  
The day does not contemplate pleasure  
The evening does not recite a hymn  
The day plays with necklaces  
Plays the sieve with rings  
The evening with glass beads  
The moon with golden rings  
I had three suitors:  
One was the moon, the second the day  
The third was full of stars  
I will not go to the moon,  
Nor go to the day  
The moon has three duties:  
Sometimes it rises early  
Once it rises at dawn's gold  
Once in the middle of dawn  
Let the starry one come  
With horses full of stars  
With clothes full of stars  
The star softly shakes  
Rings with golden sparkle  
Bring my own tub  
Drive me to Salme’s manor.", 'What lulls this sleep to rest,  
What tethers the act of sleeping.  
Sleep does not grant new growth to the moon,  
Sleeping clothes the earth.  
Sleep sends one wandering,  
Sleeping sends one marching,  
Treading a path ahead.  
Those who sleep are fire starters,  
Those who sleep are house keepers,  
The slave child does not sleep soundly:  
comes tired from work,  
comes weary from the field,  
withered from the haystack...']

Name: 5_prayer_maiden_words_stone
Representative_Docs:
['Always I am wretched  
How many times has my mind been sad  
To whom do I complain my sorrow  
To whom do I plant boredom  
To whom do I place wretchedness  
On the stone on the church path  
On the rope on the priest’s field  
The stone does not understand the maiden’s denial  
The rock does not heed the maiden’s prayer  
The proud stone did not speak  
But the thick rock did not tell.', 'If I were to sing, I would be criticized  
If I were silent, I would be sworn at,  
If I sat, it would be boring,  
If I stepped, it would be pitiful.  
To those whose minds are sad:  
I complain under the goldfinch,  
I grow like the bluebells,  
On the stones, on the church path,  
On the altar of the priest.  
The stone does not understand the maiden’s mind,  
The limestone does not heed the maiden’s prayer.  
The stone does not speak loudly,  
The thick limestone does not tell tales,  
The stone does not talk to anyone.', "Always I am sorrowful  
Every night is tedious  
Every day is long  
To whom do I plant boredom  
To whom do I set sorrow  
To whom do I complain a sad mind  
To the stone on the church path  
To the rope outside the pasture  
The stone does not speak  
The thick limestone does not tell  
The stone does not understand a maiden's language  
The limestone does not understand a maiden's prayer  
Little stone, dear stone  
Little limestone, thick little one  
You could roar in the sea  
Shout on the seashores  
Move in the sea's sand  
Could bounce on the sea bottom  
Before you came to our land  
To our yard for torment  
To the crook of the arm for suffering  
Our yards are thin  
Shoulders are slender  
If my yards were rowanberry  
Shoulders were apple tree  
Fingers crushed currants  
Then I should endure the whip  
Bear the club  
Answer with the rod."]
